purpose: Task B preparation: the wide decoder lanes' clock on an UltraScale+ part, as an estimate for AWS F2's VU47P, which the free Vivado licence does not cover
f2_clocks: clk_main_a0 fixed at 250 MHz; recipe clocks include 225 (B2), 200 (C1, C3), 187.5 (A0) and 150 MHz (C1); own MMCMs allowed (F2 Clock Recipes User Guide)
stand_in_part: xcku5p-ffvb676-2-e: Kintex UltraScale+, the same -2 speed grade; covered by the free Vivado Basic licence (2026.1 tier table)
tool: Vivado 2026.1 (Vivado Basic licence), out of context, model/perf/probes/usplus_timing.tcl: place ExtraTimingOpt, phys_opt AggressiveExplore, route AggressiveExplore, post-route phys_opt AggressiveExplore (as build_batch.tcl with VIVADO_EFFORT=high); each stage a separate process capped at 9 GB

designs.1: usplus_batch_top.sv: one lane (bench_lane.sv, FAST=2) in the batched harness (uart_batch_core.sv), as on the board; one synthesis
designs.15: usplus_lanes_top.sv: 15 lanes (bench_lane.sv, FAST=2) with registered inputs and folded outputs, without the UART core; one lane synthesized on its own (stage lane) and its netlist placed in all 15
designs.24: usplus_lanes_top.sv with 24 lanes (72 % of the KU5P's LUTs, about the Artix-7 batch's 68 %), filled from the 15-lane run's lane netlist
designs.1 at 3.75 ns: as the one-lane run, at 266.67 MHz (AWS clock recipe C3)

period_ns: 4.0 (250 MHz, F2's main clock); one run at 3.75 (266.67 MHz)
result: one lane: 250 MHz met (+0.573 ns) and 266.67 MHz met (+0.453 ns); 15 lanes at 250 MHz: met, +0.061 ns overall (a lane's reset fan-out, routing only), +0.336 ns inside the decoders; 24 lanes at 250 MHz: met, +0.043 ns overall (a lane's FIFO pointer to its clock gate's enable), +0.117 ns inside the decoders. The decoders' worst path is always the Huffman decoder's bit window and code table. Hold is met but tight in every run (+0.010 to +0.019 ns).

comparison_artix7.xc7a200tfbg484-2, 15 lanes: 141.5 MHz (-0.399 ns at 150 MHz, every lane on the Huffman bit-window loop)

side_finding.symptom: uart_batch_core.sv with 15 lanes passes 9 GB in synthesis on the KU5P even with the lanes as black boxes (killed twice at the cap; -resource_sharing off did not help); one lane in it needs 3.5 GB. The Artix-7 batch build's 11.2 GB synthesis peak came from the same core.
side_finding.cause: the result selection in process p_tx: a loop over the lanes that, for the first ready lane, assigns the whole 256-bit result record (and sent_r[i], tsend, ti) inside the loop body; each iteration's assignment overrides the previous ones, and Vivado's RTL Optimization Phase 2 spends most of the memory and time on those 15 chained 256-bit assignments
side_finding.experiment: uart_batch_core alone, N=15, lanes as black boxes (model/perf/probes/usplus_lane_stub.sv), synth_design out of context, 4 threads; variants of the core differing only as listed

results_xc7a200tfbg484-2.original: 5.4 GB peak, RTL Optimization Phase 2 ends at 1:51 and 5.1 GB, 3.2 min in all, 1,843 LUTs, 1,396 registers
results_xc7a200tfbg484-2.result by index: the loop only finds the: 2.9 GB peak, Phase 2 ends at 0:41 and 2.5 GB, 2.2 min, 1,492 LUTs, 1,396 registers

side_finding.fix_not_applied: boards/acorn_cle215/uart_batch_core.sv is unchanged (it is the board-verified harness); the result-by-index form is functionally the same and would need the batch simulation re-run before use

caveats: a stand-in: the VU47P has three SLRs (dies) and the AWS shell takes part of it; SLR crossings, the shell and its memory interfaces are not modelled
the 15 lanes fill 45 % and the 24 lanes 72 % of the KU5P's LUTs (68 % on the Artix-7 batch); the VU47P with the shell would hold more
out of context: the clock enters on a port that drives a BUFG and one BUFGCE per lane; on F2 it comes from the shell
a timing estimate only: no board, no bitstream

stages.lane: the 15-lane run's lane.edf (same lane, same 4.0 ns)
